startScreen.title: 36 Questions
description: The questions gradually become more personal.
Take turns, answer with specific examples, and pass when needed.

endScreen.title: Experiment Completed
endScreen.subtitle: Closeness is not a result screen. Notice what you now want to ask next.

questions.question: Who shaped your idea of a good life, and what would you ask them over dinner?
more: Think about historical figures, celebrities, or people you admire
Share the reason why you chose this person
Describe the topics you want to discuss with them

questions.question: If strangers knew your name, what would you want it to be for?
Which conversations make you rehearse, and what are you trying to control?
Describe a genuinely good day, including the ordinary parts.
When do you sing, hum, or make noise without caring how it sounds?
As you age, which would you fight harder to protect: your body's freedom or your mind's clarity?
How does knowing your life is finite change the way you spend an ordinary week?
Name three ways the two of you are more alike than you expected.
What are you grateful for that you rarely remember to name?
Which rule from your upbringing are you still trying to unlearn?
Tell your life story through five moments that changed its direction.
What ability would change your daily life more than it would impress anyone?
What truth about your future would you choose not to know?
Which dream have you kept alive mostly by postponing it?
What achievement cost you more than people could see?
What behavior makes a friendship feel safe enough to last?
Which memory do you return to when you need proof that life can feel good?
Which memory still has more influence over you than you want it to?
If you had one year left, what would stop receiving your time immediately?
Complete this sentence: Friendship is something you do when...
Which emotion gets the most room in your life, and which gets the least?
Take turns naming three specific things you appreciate about how the other person moves through the world.
What did your family make easy to express, and what did it make difficult?
Which caregiver taught you the most about closeness, for better or worse?
Make three true sentences beginning with: Right now, we...
Complete this sentence: I want someone I can share...
If we became close, what would I need to understand about you sooner rather than later?
Name something you like about the other person that only became visible through attention.
Share an awkward moment that became funny only after enough time passed.
When did you last cry with someone present, and when did you hide it?
Which quality in the other person surprised you as this conversation unfolded?
What subject should never become a joke at someone else's expense?
What important sentence are you still postponing, and who needs to hear it?
If you could rescue one object from your home after everyone was safe, what would it carry for you?
Which family story or ritual do you most want to keep alive?
Share one real problem. Ask the other person to reflect what they hear before offering any solution.
